subject: SLA: uptime ladder & monthly credit calculation

Subject: SLA: uptime ladder and monthly credits — clarification

Vanessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement wants one clear, example-driven paragraph for how monthly credits are calculated so they can include it in the SOW. Two quick clarifications: 1) If we hit a partial-month outage (e.g., 2 hours in a 30-day month), do you prorate by minutes or by incident buckets? 2) For latency breaches (p95), do you treat that as a separate credit pool or fold it into the uptime calculation?

Attached is a short doc with our questions (Acme-SLA-questions.docx). Can you send a concrete formula and one worked example with numbers? Also include the maximum monthly credit cap and timing of payment (credit on invoice vs cash payout).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 20-min call if easier.

—Jordan

Head of Platform Procurement, Acme Corp
jordan.price@acme.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime ladder and monthly credits — clarification

Jordan — thanks for the specific ask. Below is a compact, machine-readable explanation we use internally plus a worked example. I'm also attaching a CSV with the step-by-step calculation and bands (SLA-formula-sheet.csv) and a link to a sample invoice showing how credits appear.

High-level policy (short): monthly credit = prorated minutes of eligible downtime multiplied by the monthly committed fee, subject to band multipliers for severity and a monthly cap. Latency breaches are handled by a separate latency-bucket that converts measured p95 excess into an equivalent minute-weight (latency multiplier) before applying the same credit math. Credits are issued as invoice credits applied to the next billing cycle unless otherwise negotiated.

Formal formula (read left-to-right):
- eligible_downtime_minutes = sum of minutes where service was unavailable (excluding scheduled maintenance windows and agreed regional carveouts)
- base_credit = (eligible_downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_commitment_amount
- severity_multiplier = 1.0 for standard outages, 1.5 for partial-degradation incidents (major loss of capacity), 2.0 for full service-loss incidents beyond X minutes
- latency_equivalent_minutes = latency_excess_score * latency_conversion_factor (details in attached CSV)
- adjusted_credit = base_credit * severity_multiplier + ((latency_equivalent_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_commitment_amount)
- final_credit = min(adjusted_credit, monthly_cap_percent * monthly_commitment_amount)

Worked example (30-day month, total_minutes_in_month = 43,200):
- monthly_commitment_amount = $120,000
- observed eligible_downtime_minutes = 120 (2 hours)
- base_credit = (120 / 43,200) * $120,000 = 0.002777... * $120,000 = $333.33
- severity_multiplier = 1.0 (standard outage) => $333.33
- latency breach: p95 exceeded threshold for equivalent of 30 latency_minutes (converted via latency formula) => latency_credit = (30 / 43,200) * $120,000 = $83.33
- adjusted_credit = $333.33 + $83.33 = $416.66
- monthly_cap_percent = 25% => cap = 0.25 * $120,000 = $30,000
- final_credit = min($416.66, $30,000) = $416.66

Payment timing: credits are applied as a dollar invoice credit on the next invoice cycle by default. For enterprise contracts that require cash settlement, we can add a clause for net-30 cash payout upon acceptance of the credit calculation.

Notes and edge cases:
- Partial-month proration is minute-level; we do not use incident buckets unless mutually agreed for legacy customers.
- Scheduled maintenance windows (published in advance) are excluded; emergency maintenance required for security patches is eligible for exclusion if we've notified within the agreed SLA window.
- We track latency and availability separately but allow combined remediation (as above) if both occur in the same incident.

If this aligns with Acme's procurement needs, Ben can draft the exact SOW wording and Laura can confirm the enterprise cap and invoicing language for the first-year pilot. Happy to jump on a call to run through a few more numerical scenarios.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Commercial Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Vanessa — this is really helpful, thank you. A couple follow-ups so we can close internally:
1) Can you confirm the definition of "eligible_downtime_minutes" for brief transient errors (e.g., 5–10 second API 500 spikes that resolve automatically)? Do you aggregate by minute or by incident?
2) For the latency_conversion_factor, can you share the constants or the conversion table so our SREs can validate?
3) We prefer invoice credit but need confirmation that the credit will not be offset against future support fees — it should reduce the usage invoice only.

If you can reply with one sentence answers for each, procurement will be able to build the SOW.

—Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>

Date: 2026-11-19T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SLA: uptime ladder and monthly credits — clarification

Jordan — quick answers inline: 
1) Transient spikes: we aggregate by minute. Any minute where >=50% of calls to the primary region return 5xx is counted as an "unavailable" minute. Spikes under 60 seconds that do not affect >=50% of calls are not counted. This gives deterministic, SRE-friendly behavior.
2) Latency conversion: attached CSV (SLA-formula-sheet.csv) contains the table. High-level: each p95 breach maps to a percentile-excess score; that score is multiplied by a configured conversion factor (default 0.5) to generate latency_equivalent_minutes. We can make conversion factors explicit in the SOW; typical defaults are conservative to avoid over-crediting.
3) Credits: confirmed — invoice credits reduce the usage invoice only and will not be netted against support or professional services line items unless explicitly stated. Credits appear as a separate line item with a link to the incident summary and calculation.

Operational addendum: we recommend a 25% monthly cap for pilots, stepping down to 15% after a 12-month performance review. Credits are processed after incident validation (we share incident timeline + metrics) and are applied in the following billing cycle. Appeals window: 30 days from incident report.

If that all looks good I can work with legal to produce the exact clause language and add the latency conversion table to the appendix.

—Ben

- monthly remedy cap: 10% of the monthly commitment (invoice credits)
- minute-level proration for downtime; minute aggregation rule as Ben outlined
- separate latency band with conversion table to be included in Appendix A
- credits applied to usage invoice in the next cycle; appeal window 30 days

We will include a clause that triggers a review at month 6 to re-evaluate cap and conversion factors. Ben will provide the exact SOW text and Vanessa will circulate the DocuSign link for signature.
